rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the sūrah’s close, God gives the Prophet, and through him all Muslims, apt directives for dealing with opposition.
rows.anchor: near the end of the sūrah, some apt and appropriate directives are given to the Prophet (sws) and through him to all Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, al-ʿafw means to overlook or ignore someone, rather than to forgive inwardly.
rows.anchor: it does not mean to forgive someone by one’s heart; it rather means to ignore someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿurf denotes recognized noble practices; here it includes monotheism, the hereafter, and righteous deeds, grounded in human nature and intellect and affirmed by upright people.
rows.anchor: The actual word ¯ refers to all those practices which are regarded to be pious and noble in the eyes of all upright people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh means to inflict harm or injury.
rows.anchor: to inflict harm or injury

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should seek God’s refuge from harm; God hears his supplications, knows his worries and the mischief of devils and wrongdoers, and will dispel his sorrows.
rows.anchor: His pleadings and supplications are heard by Him and He fully knows his worries

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the command to forgive is singular, it addresses all Muslims through the Prophet, as the later plural address to the God-fearing confirms.
rows.anchor: Though the address in “forgive” is singular, but through the Prophet (sws) it is directed to all Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God gives people insight and strength, clarifying their vision so they can see reality.
rows.anchor: this remembrance will create such insight and strength in them that their vision will become absolutely clear and they will see the reality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “brothers” are the compatriots who influence the heedless, whether devils among jinn or human beings; “these” refers back to the ignorant in 7:199.
rows.anchor: The antecedent of the pronoun “these” in “brothers of these” are the “ignorant” mentioned in verse 199.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts the disbelievers’ recurring taunts when the Prophet does not produce a demanded miracle.
rows.anchor: The implication is that when the Prophet (sws) does not show them a miracle at their demand they taunt him by asking

rows.speaker: the wrongdoers
rows.claim: They imply that the Qur’an is easily assembled from earlier peoples’ stories and traditions of soothsayers and the People of the Book, then falsely presented as revelation.
rows.anchor: What these wrongdoers would imply through this statement was that as far as the Qur’ ān is concerned, its matter is quite simple

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt goes beyond failure to show a miracle: its more poisonous charge is that the Qur’an is fabricated by selecting material from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: the blame of not being able to show a miracle but a more poisonous blame in it is that, God forbid, the Qur’ ān is a fabrication

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ literally means selecting something from an assortment.
rows.anchor: The word إﺟﺘﺒﺎءliterally means “to choose and select a thing from an assortment.”

rows.speaker: Al-Farrā’
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also interprets ijtibāʾ in its sarcastic context as meaning “to fabricate.”
rows.anchor: Al-Farr ā’ has also interpreted the word in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that he follows what his Lord reveals answers the sarcasm and exemplifies ignoring the ignorant rather than engaging their foolish banter.
rows.anchor: is an answer to this sarcasm. Earlier, the Prophet (sws) was also asked to disregard the ignorance of the ignorant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is guidance with respect to people’s beginning and mercy with respect to their end.
rows.anchor: They are guidance with regard to the beginning and mercy with regard to the end.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for those who believe” subtly indicates that the revelation is sound; the shortcoming lies in hearts unwilling to believe.
rows.anchor: whatever the Prophet (sws) is presenting has no shortcoming; it is their hearts which really fall short because they do not want to believe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening attentively and remaining silent is the way to benefit from the Qur’an’s guidance and insight.
rows.anchor: states the way to benefit from the guidance and insight provided by the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also condemns disbelievers’ noisy response, which reflects ignorance and deprives them of mercy; attentive listening is the right response and brings mercy.
rows.anchor: The correct attitude is totally opposite to it: they should listen intently instead of making noise.

rows.speaker: some jurists
rows.claim: Some jurists cite this verse to support reciting Sūrah al-Fātiḥah behind the prayer leader.
rows.anchor: our jurists also presents this verse in support of their view

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the verse has another context and its wording instead supports reciting al-Fātiḥah in silent prayers, not loud ones.
rows.anchor: in the loud prayers S ūrah al-Fātiḥah should not be recited while in the silent prayers, it should be recited.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance should be inward, humble, meek, and fearful; arrogance and conceit are its opposites.
rows.anchor: it should be in one’s heart and should be with humility, meekness and fear.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If remembrance is audible, it should be moderate, as 17:110 directs; this also avoids adopting the idolaters’ way, since God hears and knows all.
rows.anchor: do not offer your prayer very loudly or in a very low tone; adopt a middle way between the two.

rows.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: The Prophet once stopped his companions from praying aloud.
rows.anchor: on one occasion, the Prophet (sws) had stopped his companions from praying in a loud voice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loud prayer can lead to pretension and showing off, both contrary to sincerity.
rows.anchor: this may lead to pretension and showing off, which are totally against sincerity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Morning and evening” comprehensively covers all times, and the warning against indifference reinforces that remembrance should be continuous.
rows.anchor: The words “morning and evening” are meant to comprehensively cover all times.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As breathing sustains bodily life, remembrance sustains the soul; it is essential protection because Satan is always ready to attack.
rows.anchor: Just as for the life of the body, breathing is essential, in the same way, for the life of the soul, God’s remembrance is essential.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of remembrance may change with circumstances and needs, but it must never be forgotten, even for a moment, lest Satan attack.
rows.anchor: The form of this remembrance changes with circumstances and needs but it is not permissible to forget it at any instant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though singular in form, the address denotes a plural audience, as in verse 199.
rows.anchor: Though the address of the verse is in the singular, it denotes plurality, as in verse 199 earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last verse refers to angels, who never disdain worship and glorify and prostrate before God.
rows.anchor: This refers to the angels.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who continually remember and praise God on earth are spiritually joined to the angelic assembly, which likewise glorifies and praises Him.
rows.anchor: This is because just as the latter are constantly glorifying and praising God, these people too are doing so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes idolaters who arrogantly expect angels to intercede for them while giving little importance to God and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: they show arrogance because they think that they will receive intercession from angels

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels themselves continually glorify and prostrate before God, challenging the idolaters’ presumption about angelic intercession.
rows.anchor: such is the state of these angels that they are constantly glorifying and prostrating before God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion turns to Jewish conspiracies and the mischief of hypocrites and jealous elements.
rows.anchor: conspiracies of Jews, the mischief worked by the hypocrites and jealous elements is now referred to.

rows.speaker: the disbelievers
rows.claim: They say the believers’ religion has made them irrational for thinking that a small force can face a much larger army.
rows.anchor: the disbelievers contended that the believers think that in spite of their small number, they could take on the huge army of their enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such demoralizing remarks are especially influential when made by people from the believers’ own faction; scarce resources could worsen their effect, but God protected the believers.
rows.anchor: When such sentences are uttered in particular by people belonging to their own faction, the believers were bound to be influenced by them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who trusted God and advanced saw His power and wisdom; He supports those who trust Him, cannot be defeated, and directs a strategy no one can overcome.
rows.anchor: those who trusted God and proceeded for the onslaught saw from their own eyes that God is Powerful and Wise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s defeat is only the first warning; the greater punishment is imminent when they face death.
rows.anchor: the defeat the Quraysh have faced is just the first instalment of warning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not remove a nation’s favor until it changes inwardly: He warns it first, then decisively punishes continued rebellion, as with Pharaoh’s people after trials failed to reform them.
rows.anchor: He does not deprive a nation of His favours until it adopts a wrong attitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most vile people are adamant disbelievers who refuse belief and repeatedly break their promises.
rows.anchor: the filthiest people are those have become adamant on disbelief and did not profess belief. They repeatedly break their promises.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet and his companions meet such people in battle, they should rout them so thoroughly that their supporters take warning.
rows.anchor: they should rout them to such an extent that those who are supporting them also learn a lesson

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If treachery is feared, the agreement should be returned to the other party on equal terms, since God dislikes the treacherous.
rows.anchor: those about whom the fear any breach of promise, they should throw it back on them because God does not like those who break promises.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the conditional sentence about seeing the angels take souls, the answer is omitted for eloquence because the scene’s heinousness exceeds words.
rows.anchor: The answer to the conditional clause “and if you would have been able to see …” is suppressed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial formed against an exaggerated charge intensifies the negation, emphasizing that God does not wrong His servants.
rows.anchor: the negation on the exaggerated statement is meant to exaggerate the negation.
